2
Gm, Tm, m and pm are all units of length.
Which unit is the largest and which unit is the smallest?

largest

hints: Look at the SI prefixes in front of m: G, T, $\mu$ and p - the size of the unit is set by the power of 10 for each prefix.
Recall that for large prefixes $\text{T}$ means $10^{12}$ and $\text{G}$ means $10^9$, so one of these gives a length larger than $10^9 \text{ m}$.
Recall that for small prefixes $\mu$ means $10^{-6}$ and $\text{p}$ means $10^{-12}$, so compare $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ with $10^{-12} \text{ m}$ to find the smaller length.
walkthrough: Identify the base unit and prefixes: all four are metres multiplied by an SI prefix - G for giga, T for tera, $\mu$ for micro and p for pico.
State the prefix values: $1 \text{ Gm} = 10^9 \text{ m}$, $1 \text{ Tm} = 10^{12} \text{ m}$, $1 \, \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and $1 \text{ pm} = 10^{-12} \text{ m}$.
Compare the two large units: $10^{12} > 10^9$, so $1 \text{ Tm}$ is $1000$ times larger than $1 \text{ Gm}$ and is the largest unit.
Compare the two small units: $10^{-12} < 10^{-6}$, so $1 \text{ pm}$ is $10^6$ times smaller than $1 \, \mu\text{m}$ and is the smallest unit.
Combine the results: largest is Tm and smallest is pm. This is option D.

A.explanation: $\text{Gm}$ is not the largest because $10^9$ is smaller than $10^{12}$, and $\mu\text{m}$ is not the smallest because $10^{-6}$ is larger than $10^{-12}$.

B.explanation: $\text{pm}$ is the smallest, but $\text{Gm}$ is not the largest because tera is $10^{12}$ while giga is only $10^9$.

C.explanation: $\text{Tm}$ is the largest, but $\mu\text{m}$ is not the smallest because micro $10^{-6}$ is much larger than pico $10^{-12}$.

D.explanation: $\text{Tm} = 10^{12} \text{ m}$ is the largest and $\text{pm} = 10^{-12} \text{ m}$ is the smallest of the four prefixes.
